priorAbsorption: PINT-T0 through PINT-T3 (2026-06-28) already closed a representative-scan absorption of this same retained folder: T0 audited and relocated it, T1 mapped concepts to Model Gateway/provider-lane owner surfaces, T2 promoted a CVF-owned claim-boundary and receipt-advisory reference, and T3 closed the static-checker lane with no checker now. PINT-R1 is a full 50-file individual-content rescan of the same corpus that recovers additional doctrine-level candidates (fail-closed unavailability menu, granular weighting tiers, concrete task-type/capability vocabulary, receipt proves/does-not-prove split, probe-only-insufficient-for-freeze sentence, five additional risk rows) without reopening T0-T3's closed decisions or the EAIC knowledge-gap map's PARKED_KNOWLEDGE_GAP position.

findings.summary: Ten source-backed candidate rows were independently reviewed: six were retained as advisory knowledge in the governed audit, two were deferred pending current-owner source verification, and two were closed as no-new-value variants.
findings.nextAction: No automatic owner edit. Reopen the two source-verification candidates only under the concrete conditions in the Reviewer Semantic Value Decision table; other accepted advisory knowledge remains discoverable in the audit.

findings.summary: All EAIC-adjacent doctrine in this corpus (dev-MCP boundary, fail-closed language, risk register) was individually tested against the EAIC knowledge-gap map's nine-domain matrix and confirmed to supply no primary-source class the map does not already list as missing.
findings.nextAction: None. The EAIC map's PARKED_KNOWLEDGE_GAP position and acquisition-priority table remain unchanged.

findings.summary: An earlier worker pass on this tranche independently re-implemented the manifest content-hash recipe and produced a digest that did not match the GC-018 baseline, even though its enumeration and path-sort logic were verified correct; only running the GC-018's own embedded canonical script reproduced the baseline value.
findings.nextAction: Future digest-bearing GC-018/work-order packets should embed a directly runnable canonical hashing script (as this GC-018 now does) rather than only a prose recipe description, so independent re-implementations cannot silently diverge.
